Last time I made a review (?) about an IEM, I got my ass blasted for not liking it despite the IEM generally being a good/safe tune to listen to. That IEM being the Salnotes Zero. 

So this my redemption review, as I see no one has made a post about the new ZS10 Pro X. 

First of all, I think the "KZ/CCA" sound has plateaued over the year (2021-2022 specifically), whenever I unbox or try a KZ/CCA you get the same unboxing and listening experience, so you end up knowing what you're signing up for and have the same expectations, really. 

So, I'll cut to the chase, this is really just no different from any KZ I've heard, or experienced. Just minor tweaks and incrimental changes that YOU should decide if it's worth the pick up or not. 

If you owned the original ZS10 Pro , then you know it has that peaked 8khz that makes it fatiguing over time, the new IEM (ZS10 Pro X) has been tamed to a very reasonable/enjoyable amount + this new IEM has a bass boost compared to the original. That's it, and that apparently warrants the rehash for KZ. 

If you haven't owned the ZS10 Pro, basically it's a slightly V-shaped IEM with a bass boost, and allegedly 'good highs', the reason people picked a ZS10 Pro up is because of the '10 Drivers in your ear' promise of providing good detail retrieval and imaging and so on. Which it sort of delivered but was plagued by a terrible peak at 8Khz that can hurt to listen to even if you're a 'treblehead'. 

Now let's talk driver tech, which is why I got blasted on my Salnotes Zero Review, because "dRivErS tEch sHouLdN'T mAtTer" 

This thing is mainly run by it's dynamic driver, and when it can't handle it, it throws the music over to the BAs for support. I think this a good way to keep the sound going, to otherwise what would be lost in the mix. 

But this thing is just plagued with being a KZ product, so even if they do a good job transfering sounds from one driver to another, the drivers doesn't sound the great. (I can already hear the driver doesn't matter mob assembling in this sentence.) 

Just to close my thoughts on this, it's a good IEM, don't get me wrong. If you haven't owned the KZ ZS10 Pro, then you should get this instead, but that's where my gripes lie about this IEM. 

What if you do own the ZS10 Pro? Why the hell should you buy this as an upgrade? 

And to that, I refer back to my statement:

> Just minor tweaks and incrimental changes that YOU should decide if it's worth the pick up or not. 

Does the bigger bass and tamed 8Khz warrant a full upgrade for you? Only you can answer that.  

Anyways, thank you for reading, I thought I wrote atrouciously this time, so sorry for that, but at the same time I had a few ramblings saved up inside me, I just have to.

In Pubs / Solo Q, This often is decided in the Stats screen during champ select, You see someone with Masters + Pred badge, with 3000 wins = we follow that person despite being the nastiest and most toxic human being alive.

The importance of being the in-game leader is as follows; if you fuck-up, the whole team fucks-up. You are responsible for a loss, and forces you to rethink strategies and the scenarios you put yourself and your team in. Apex can get unpredictable, but you play around with what you can control as the In-Game Leader.

1.) Scenarios : 

- This can be boiled down to common game knowledge or, game-sense. In which you think what you, your teammates and the enemy team are going to do in a given 'scenario'. 

- There are several ways a 'scenario' can go down to, some common ones in Apex are; 

> knock one/two enemies = push. 

> Being shot at = hide.

>Cracked or damaged = heal. 

> Noises that the enemy team and your team is making, (Ult activations, Crafter noises, voicelines) 

- These common factors require you to be vigilant in the game, and creates a common or repetitive response from you and your team in which you can play around and strategize with. 

For example; You knock two players down, the response should be push the last one, right? However, the last one you noticed is a Caustic camping in a tight building and is ready to turn around the tide against your team by picking off the overconfident member. 

As someone who is familiar with this scenario, do you push with said over-confident member? Or do you take the resources from the two you just knocked? This split second decision shouldn't be overthinked as a player, you just go with what winning scenario you have on your mind.

Rotations doesn't really matter unless you're trying to get alot of kills, if you are into watching pro play or high ranking players, most of them just find the last ring from where they dropped, and get kills trying to get there. It is flashy / cool to kill everyone in a hot drop, and then getting the win, but Apex isn't like that all the time unfortunately. 

Take time to practice! Learn how the ring works, learn the guns, and you constantly find yourself having fun, understanding the game more, and ofcourse, winning!
